You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:

CREATE TABLE continents (
    ContId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Continent TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE countries (
    CountryId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    CountryName TEXT,
    Continent INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Continent) REFERENCES continents(ContId)
);

CREATE TABLE car_makers (
    Id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Maker TEXT,
    FullName TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (Country) REFERENCES countries(CountryId)
);

CREATE TABLE model_list (
    ModelId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Maker INTEGER,
    Model TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Model),
    FOREIGN KEY (Maker) REFERENCES car_makers(Id)
);

CREATE TABLE car_names (
    MakeId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Model TEXT,
    Make TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (Model) REFERENCES model_list(Model)
);

CREATE TABLE cars_data (
    Id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    MPG TEXT,
    Cylinders INTEGER,
    Edispl REAL,
    Horsepower TEXT,
    Weight INTEGER,
    Accelerate REAL,
    Year INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Id) REFERENCES car_names(MakeId)
);

When you have a final SQL query to present, always wrap it in a sql markdown code fence like this:

```sql
SELECT ...
```

This makes it easy to identify your answer. Only use one ```sql fence for your final query.

Assuming “old car makers” means car makers with the earliest car records in the dataset, this query summarizes each maker by their oldest recorded car year:

```sql
SELECT
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName,
    c.CountryName,
    ct.Continent,
    MIN(cd.Year) AS earliest_car_year,
    COUNT(*) AS number_of_cars,
    ROUND(AVG(CAST(cd.MPG AS REAL)), 2) AS avg_mpg,
    ROUND(AVG(CAST(cd.Horsepower AS REAL)), 2) AS avg_horsepower,
    ROUND(AVG(cd.Weight), 2) AS avg_weight
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN countries c
    ON cm.Country = c.CountryId
JOIN continents ct
    ON c.Continent = ct.ContId
JOIN model_list ml
    ON cm.Id = ml.Maker
JOIN car_names cn
    ON ml.Model = cn.Model
JOIN cars_data cd
    ON cn.MakeId = cd.Id
GROUP BY
    cm.Id,
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName,
    c.CountryName,
    ct.Continent
ORDER BY
    earliest_car_year ASC,
    number_of_cars DESC;
```
focus on makers that made cars a long time ago

This focuses on makers that had cars in the earliest years represented in the dataset — specifically, within the first 3 years from the minimum `Year`.

```sql
WITH earliest_year AS (
    SELECT MIN(Year) AS min_year
    FROM cars_data
),
old_makers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        cm.Id
    FROM car_makers cm
    JOIN model_list ml
        ON cm.Id = ml.Maker
    JOIN car_names cn
        ON ml.Model = cn.Model
    JOIN cars_data cd
        ON cn.MakeId = cd.Id
    CROSS JOIN earliest_year ey
    WHERE cd.Year <= ey.min_year + 2
)
SELECT
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName,
    c.CountryName,
    ct.Continent,
    MIN(cd.Year) AS earliest_car_year,
    MAX(cd.Year) AS latest_car_year,
    COUNT(*) AS total_cars_recorded,
    ROUND(AVG(CAST(NULLIF(cd.MPG, '?') AS REAL)), 2) AS avg_mpg,
    ROUND(AVG(CAST(NULLIF(cd.Horsepower, '?') AS REAL)), 2) AS avg_horsepower,
    ROUND(AVG(cd.Weight), 2) AS avg_weight
FROM old_makers om
JOIN car_makers cm
    ON om.Id = cm.Id
JOIN countries c
    ON cm.Country = c.CountryId
JOIN continents ct
    ON c.Continent = ct.ContId
JOIN model_list ml
    ON cm.Id = ml.Maker
JOIN car_names cn
    ON ml.Model = cn.Model
JOIN cars_data cd
    ON cn.MakeId = cd.Id
GROUP BY
    cm.Id,
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName,
    c.CountryName,
    ct.Continent
ORDER BY
    earliest_car_year ASC,
    total_cars_recorded DESC;
```
Also, I want to ensure that some cars produced by these makers were made in 1970.

This keeps the “old maker” focus and explicitly requires that each maker has at least one car recorded in `1970`.

```sql
WITH earliest_year AS (
    SELECT MIN(Year) AS min_year
    FROM cars_data
)
SELECT
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName,
    c.CountryName,
    ct.Continent,
    MIN(cd.Year) AS earliest_car_year,
    MAX(cd.Year) AS latest_car_year,
    COUNT(*) AS total_cars_recorded,
    SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cars_made_in_1970,
    ROUND(AVG(CAST(NULLIF(cd.MPG, '?') AS REAL)), 2) AS avg_mpg,
    ROUND(AVG(CAST(NULLIF(cd.Horsepower, '?') AS REAL)), 2) AS avg_horsepower,
    ROUND(AVG(cd.Weight), 2) AS avg_weight
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN countries c
    ON cm.Country = c.CountryId
JOIN continents ct
    ON c.Continent = ct.ContId
JOIN model_list ml
    ON cm.Id = ml.Maker
JOIN car_names cn
    ON ml.Model = cn.Model
JOIN cars_data cd
    ON cn.MakeId = cd.Id
CROSS JOIN earliest_year ey
GROUP BY
    cm.Id,
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName,
    c.CountryName,
    ct.Continent
HAVING
    MIN(cd.Year) <= ey.min_year + 2
    AND SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
    earliest_car_year ASC,
    cars_made_in_1970 DESC,
    total_cars_recorded DESC;
```
I also need the names of these car makers that fit these criteria.

```sql
WITH earliest_year AS (
    SELECT MIN(Year) AS min_year
    FROM cars_data
)
SELECT
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml
    ON cm.Id = ml.Maker
JOIN car_names cn
    ON ml.Model = cn.Model
JOIN cars_data cd
    ON cn.MakeId = cd.Id
CROSS JOIN earliest_year ey
GROUP BY
    cm.Id,
    cm.Maker,
    cm.FullName
HAVING
    MIN(cd.Year) <= ey.min_year + 2
    AND SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
    cm.Maker;
```
